title: List tools
description:
Fill in four functions that work on lists of numbers. None of them may change the list they are given.

```lua-norun
sum(list)               -- the total; 0 for an empty list
largest(list)           -- the biggest value, or nil for an empty list
reversed(list)          -- a NEW list with the items in the opposite order
without(list, value)    -- a NEW list with every item equal to value left out
```

```lua-norun
sum({ 3, 4, 5 })              --> 12
largest({ 3, 9, 2 })          --> 9
reversed({ 1, 2, 3 })         --> { 3, 2, 1 }
without({ 1, 2, 1, 3 }, 1)    --> { 2, 3 }
```

solution.solution.lua:
function sum(list)
    local total = 0
    for _, v in ipairs(list) do total = total + v end
    return total
end

function largest(list)
    local best = list[1]
    for i = 2, #list do
        if list[i] > best then best = list[i] end
    end
    return best
end

function reversed(list)
    local out = {}
    for i = #list, 1, -1 do out[#out + 1] = list[i] end
    return out
end

function without(list, value)
    local out = {}
    for _, v in ipairs(list) do
        if v ~= value then out[#out + 1] = v end
    end
    return out
end

hints: Start `largest` with the first item, `list[1]`, which is already `nil` for an empty list.
For a new list, start with `local out = {}` and add with `out[#out + 1] = value`.
unitTests:
test("sum", function()
    check_eq(sum({ 3, 4, 5 }), 12)
    check_eq(sum({}), 0)
    check_eq(sum({ -2, 2.5 }), 0.5)
end)

test("largest", function()
    check_eq(largest({ 3, 9, 2 }), 9)
    check_eq(largest({ -5, -1, -9 }), -1)
    check_eq(largest({ 7 }), 7)
    check_eq(largest({}), nil)
end)

test("reversed makes a new list", function()
    local original = { 1, 2, 3, 4 }
    check_eq(reversed(original), { 4, 3, 2, 1 })
    check_eq(original, { 1, 2, 3, 4 })
    check(reversed(original) ~= original, "reversed must return a new table")
    check_eq(reversed({}), {})
end)

test("without", function()
    local original = { 1, 2, 1, 3, 1 }
    check_eq(without(original, 1), { 2, 3 })
    check_eq(original, { 1, 2, 1, 3, 1 })
    check_eq(without({ 4, 5 }, 9), { 4, 5 })
    check(without(original, 9) ~= original, "without must return a new table")
end)
